question: Th1 lymphocytes:

options.opd: They are very active against extracellular bacteria.
options.ope: They recruit neutrophils at the sites of antigen recognition.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Th1 lymphocytes -> produce interferon gamma (IFN-γ) -> involved in cell-mediated immunity -> 95% CHAIN: Th1 lymphocytes -> activate macrophages -> enhance phagocytosis -> 90% CHAIN: Th1 lymphocytes -> recruit and activate cytotoxic T cells -> enhance killing of infected cells -> 85% CHAIN: Th1 lymphocytes -> stimulate inflammation -> promote immune response against intracellular pathogens -> 80% CHAIN: Th1 lymphocytes -> do not mediate allergic diseases -> 95%
analysis: Th1 lymphocytes are a subset of T helper cells that play a crucial role in cell-mediated immunity. They primarily produce interferon gamma (IFN-γ) and are involved in activating macrophages and cytotoxic T cells to combat intracellular pathogens such as viruses and intracellular bacteria.
